chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub ibn Salim, raising it, said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not leave the food-stained towel in the house, for it is a play-pen for the devils'.
ai.seo_question: Why should food-stained towels be removed from the house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) relays the Prophet’s instruction that a towel (*mandil*) soiled with food residue (*ghamar*) should not be kept in the house, as it serves as a resting place for devils. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that physical impurities can attract spiritual entities, linking domestic hygiene to the preservation of spiritual purity and the mitigation of minor demonic influences.
